facts.claim: The Cisco CP-9951 runs DOOM natively on its ARMv6 CPU using MontaVista Linux 2.6.18_pro500, rendering to `/dev/fb1` and using `/dev/input/keypad0` for input.
The game is launched via the Applications menu, uses Freedoom Phase 2 as IWAD, and is persistently installed at `/mnt/flash2/doom-v666`.
Sound is produced locally via an 8 kHz G.711 µ-law RTP path bound to `127.0.0.1`, using a FIFO from FD 9 to UDP port 8096.
The red handset button exits DOOM cleanly and returns to the normal Cisco UI; keypad events are 16-byte Linux-style input records handled by `keyhandle.ko` and `keypad.ko`.
The project began as a streamed DOOM experience on Cthulhu, evolved to direct shell access via SSH, and was reverse-engineered to run natively on the phone.
Installation requires a deployment host at `10.1.1.1` serving FTP on port `2121`, and the phone must be rebooted to load the xinetd service at `/usr/local/etc/doom-local`.
The phone exposes multiple framebuffers (`/dev/fb0`–`/dev/fb3`) and input devices managed by Cisco’s Raven stack, with no external services required for final operation.
The project is an experimental community effort for privately owned hardware, documented in `docs/project-history.md` and field notes, and not affiliated with Cisco.
